output.title: Recovering from partial automation is a workflow decision
output.body:
If you are recovering from partial automation, do not start with “What AI can we add back?” Start with one workflow that was partly automated, then stalled, broke, or got abandoned. Invoice data entry, lead follow-up, and customer FAQ replies are different problems; bundling them together is how small automations turn into maintenance hobbies.

The decision is bounded: keep investing only if the workflow is repeatable, measurable, and frequent enough to justify the setup work. The 8–10 hours-a-week pain point is only a persona example, not a benchmark. If the underlying process has changed, a broken automation may simply need to stay broken.

A useful diagnostic question is: who approves the output? If the answer is always “me” or “a person”, AI-assisted automation may fit. If the answer is “nobody checks it” or “it runs without review”, you need explicit controls before you trust it. Human approval stays mandatory for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

The next step is manual on purpose: pick one half-broken workflow, write down in two sentences what still happens by hand and where the automation failed, then mark whether the output needs human approval. If you cannot answer that cleanly, the problem is scope, not software. If you do proceed, Bareni works inside your own tools and accounts, and finished code stays with you as policy, not magic.
